gaps.fact: Royal Tokaji, the Court's one Hungarian name: it is in the tokaj article only; no chapter names it and no question asks it.

The communist years from 1949 to 1989, when the Court says Tokaji was not made: the country overview tells the state farm story and dates it, but no chapter or question carries it. The Codex's reading (made for volume by the state, the private Aszú tradition broken) is the truer one and the Court's line should be met beside it, not copied.
Tokaji with foie gras, blue cheese and orchard tarts: the article and the digestif table give the pairings, but no question in either bank pairs Tokaji with any dish.
Tokaji is normally bottled in the 500 ml bottle: the size appears nowhere in the Codex, neither in the tokaj article, the chapters, the banks nor the bottles table, which has no 500 ml row.

courtUpdates.now: The Tokaj PDO specification was amended by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1556, published on 6 July 2026, revising classification, analytical limits, vineyard management and labelling; the aszú berry selection is unchanged, and secondary sources report Fordítás now bottled in the region and its dry form withdrawn. The Codex's Aszú figures (120 grams, 18 months in cask, puttonyos 5 or 6 optional, Eszencia at 450 grams) date from the 2013 reform and should be checked against the new text once it is read.
courtUpdates.source: Search: the trade reports of Vinetur (July 2026) and The Drinks Business (March 2026) on the EU approval of the revised Tokaj PDO rules; the regulation text itself was not returned.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 0 (no Hungarian category; the six Tokaji stems in Dessert & Sweet Wines and Sparkling/Fortified/Sweet are listed in the coverage), Village 41 (Hungary & Greece, of which 22 are Hungarian and 19 Greek), 41 in all. The Court's Tokaji cells are thoroughly taught: the Bodrog and its fog, the Zemplén hills, botrytis, puttonyos as the old hod and the modern 120 gram rule, Furmint and Hárslevelű, Eszencia as the free run of aszú berries, szamorodni, the 1737 decree and the early vineyard classes. The four thin cells are Royal Tokaji, the communist years, Tokaji at the table and the 500 ml bottle. One reading for the owner: the Court's History & Lore cell says Tokaji was not made between 1949 and 1989, while the Codex says the state farm made it for volume; the Codex is right and should keep its line. One inconsistency inside the Codex, not an error: the temperature table serves Tokaji with the sweet whites at 6 to 8 C while the tokaj article says 10 to 12; both are defensible, but a candidate should meet one figure or a reason for two. No factual error found in the Hungarian material. One search spent, on the 2026 amendment of the Tokaj PDO; the second was not needed.
